provenance.instrument: East Norriton Township Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 205 Zoning, Ord. No. 96 of 9-11-1973, readopted 12-20-2005 by Ord. No. 484 and 1-7-2008 by Ord. No. 504, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 EA1154, Township of East Norriton, Montgomery County. Chapter 205 was adopted 9-11-1973 by Ord. No. 96 and readopted in 2005 and 2008. The relative quarters rule is in 205-16B(4), uses accessory to a dwelling. New Laws lists Ord. No. 591 to 611 (2021 to 2026), none of them amending Chapter 205. The township's own ordinance list for 600 to 699 shows no zoning amendment either
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360: 'Includes legislation adopted through 06-29-2021.' New Laws lists no zoning ordinance after that date
checks: Relative quarters are an accessory use to a dwelling: 'Neither the present structure nor the proposed addition shall at any time be occupied by any person other than the property owner and members of his or her immediate family' (205-16B(4)(a))

'In-law quarters must be located in the existing dwelling or must be attached to the existing dwelling, and there shall always be maintained the standard doorway and/or passageway connecting the principal residence and the in-law quarters. In-law quarters shall not be located in a separate freestanding building' (205-16B(4)(e))
The owner may not lease or rent the quarters, files a deed restriction with the Recorder of Deeds, and holds a one-year renewable permit from the Zoning Officer (205-16B(4)(c), (f), (g))

On a sale the property passes as a single-family dwelling. Unless the deed restriction is filed and the new owner keeps the relative quarters, any second kitchen must be removed before the sale (205-16B(4)(b), (d))
An accessory building is 'not to be used as a dwelling unit unless such building was originally designed as a dwelling unit, as in conjunction with an institution' (205-5 'Building, accessory')
The code sets no size cap and no parking figure for relative quarters. Two off-street spaces per dwelling unit, a garage not counted (205-102A)
In the ECII residential section 'Uses permitted in § 205-16 are strictly prohibited with the exception of an attached garage' (205-63.12A)
Family: related persons living as one nonprofit housekeeping unit 'doing their cooking on the premises on a single cooking facility', plus two gratuitous guests (205-5 'Family')
A lot of record too small for the district may get a variance from the Zoning Hearing Board. Where all requirements but lot area are met, the Zoning Officer may permit a permitted use (205-12)
No section read bars a use variance. Variances need the five MPC hardship findings and lapse after one year without a building permit (205-142E, J)

Twins and townhouses in CR may hold relative quarters, since the code defines them as single-family attached or semidetached dwellings. Whether duplexes and multiplexes in CR may is not settled (205-36A, 205-16B(4))

Near the airport: anyone who plans 'to add to an existing structure ... in the vicinity of the airport' must first file PennDOT Form AV-57 and include the response with the permit application (205-180A)
'Alterations, conversion' means 'A multifamily dwelling constructed by converting an existing dwelling into apartments for more than one family' (205-5). No district lists it as a use
The sewer charge is set per equivalent dwelling unit, so an added unit may owe a further charge (Chapter 18, 18-15C). Rental units need a license under Chapter 159
provenance.notes: Zoning office: East Norriton Township. Read in a browser on eCode360, one page at a time, on 2026-11-15, in print view. Searched the code (scope all) for accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, accessory suite, ECHO, elder cottage, granny, guest house, carriage house, tenant house, living quarters, second dwelling, conversion, two-family, caretaker, farm dwelling, relative and servants. The search did not return 205-16B(4), which says 'Relative quarters' and 'in-law quarters'. It was found by reading Article IV. Read: Article II (205-4, 205-5), Article III, Article IV (205-11 to 205-22.5), the district articles for AR, BR, BR-1, MR, GA, CR, HR, HR-1, RP, RO, IN, BP, EC, ECII, C, C-1, SC, I, LI, R-R, HI and ATR, Article XVIII (parking) and Article XXII (Zoning Hearing Board). Not read: Article I, XVII (floodplain), XIX (signs), XX (nonconforming uses), XXI (administration), XXIII (heliports), XXIV, XXVIII (airport overlay, apart from the 205-180A permit step), XXIX (wireless) and the PDF attachment 205a Minimum Lot Dimensions (CR lots). 205-6 lists the district as RR, its article is titled R-R. Most districts permit their listed uses 'and no other'. R-R (205-152) does not use those words. RO permits by conditional use 'uses which are similar to those in § 205-54.2 above' (205-54.3A), and 205-54.2 lists the two-family detached dwelling. RP permits similar offices by conditional use (205-47A(1)), not dwellings. C, C-1, SC, I, LI and HI allow uses of the same general character as listed ones by special exception. BR-1 permits a townhouse or twin house development by conditional use on 60,000 sq ft (205-30.2B). AR permits smaller cluster lots in a subdivision of 80 acres or more (205-26). The Township has a historic preservation chapter (Ch. 11) that was not read. No general accessory building setback rule was found in the sections read, apart from MR (205-30.7G(4)) and the accessory heights in each district. Districts in doubt, and why: C-1 permits a single-family detached dwelling under the BR figures (205-66.2A(9)), but its accessory use listing (7) reaches only the uses listed above it and does not name 205-16. RR permits any RP use, so a house with 205-16B accessory uses, only by special exception (205-152C(2)). GA, HR and HR-1 list 'Accessory uses in accordance with § 205-16' but permit only apartment houses, and 205-16B(4)(b) has the property sold as a single-family dwelling. IN lists 'Accessory uses as defined in § 205-16' (205-56J), but its only homes are churches 'and their adjunct residential dwellings' (205-56A) and hospital temporary living quarters for patients' families.

term.note: 'Relative quarters, subject to the following conditions'. The conditions also call them 'in-law quarters'. Listed among the uses accessory to a dwelling

status.note: Only the property owner and members of his or her immediate family may occupy the house and the quarters. A zoning permit from the Zoning Officer, renewed each year

scope_districts.note: AR, BR and BR-1 permit 'Accessory uses in accordance with § 205-16', MR and CR the same, RP and RO 'Single-family detached dwellings and accessory uses in accordance with § 205-16B'. CR permits no detached house, only townhouses, twins, duplexes and multiplexes

status_outside.note: BP, EC, C, SC, I, LI, HI and ATR list no house with 205-16 accessory uses. Most of them permit their listed uses 'and no other'

value.note: 'Uses permitted in § 205-16 are strictly prohibited with the exception of an attached garage' in the ECII residential section

status_by_form.note: 'In-law quarters shall not be located in a separate freestanding building.' An accessory building is 'not to be used as a dwelling unit unless such building was originally designed as a dwelling unit, as in conjunction with an institution' (205-5)

path.note: 'A one-year renewable permit issued by the Township Zoning Officer shall be required to ensure compliance with this chapter.' No hearing is named. The fee is set by resolution

fallback_path.note: Five findings of unnecessary hardship. No section read bars a use variance. A variance lapses after one year without a building permit (205-142J)

value.name: Two-family detached dwelling (RO)
value.conditions: 'Two-family detached dwellings' are a permitted use in RO. A two-family dwelling is 'A building designed for and occupied exclusively as a dwelling for two families' (205-5). Lot 20,000 sq ft, 100 ft wide, front 50 ft, side 20 ft (30 ft next to a residential district), rear 100 ft, building coverage 15%, impervious 30%. Two off-street spaces per dwelling unit, a garage not counted (205-102A). 'A use must utilize an existing building for its purposes unless a conditional use approval has been granted' (205-54.5A)
value.note: The code sets no lot area per unit in RO, so the 20,000 sq ft lot holds both units. A new building needs a conditional use from the Board of Supervisors

value.name: Duplex or twin house in an MR development
value.conditions: MR permits twin houses and duplexes. The district needs a tract of at least five developable acres, public sewer and water, at most five dwelling units per gross acre, 4,000 sq ft of lot per dwelling unit (5,500 on average), and two off-street spaces per unit. Twin and duplex figures: front yard 25 ft on average across the development (half of a front facade may stand 20 ft back), rear yard 30 ft, side yard 10 ft (one side only for a twin), building coverage 35%, height 35 ft and two stories (205-30.6, 205-30.7)
value.note: A development standard for the whole tract. Whether an existing house lot in an MR development may be changed into a duplex is not settled. Ask the zoning officer

value.name: Duplex or twin house in a CR development
value.conditions: CR permits townhouses, twin houses, duplexes and multiplexes on a lot of at least five acres, with public sewer and water, at most six duplex units or five twin units per developable acre, two off-street spaces per unit (a garage not counted) and at least 650 sq ft of living area per unit (205-36, 205-38, 205-39)
value.note: The CR minimum lot dimensions are in a PDF attachment (205a) that was not read

value.name: One more dwelling unit at or above the second story (RP)
value.conditions: 'Accessory uses on the same lot with and customarily incidental to any of the above permitted uses, including one dwelling unit, provided that such use shall be located at or above the second story' (205-46I). The first use listed above is 'Single-family detached dwellings and accessory uses in accordance with § 205-16B' (205-46A). Lot 10,000 sq ft with sanitary sewer. Two off-street spaces per dwelling unit (205-102A)
value.note: Read literally, a house in RP may hold one more dwelling unit at or above the second story, by right and with no family rule. This conflicts with 205-16B(4), which lets a house hold only relative quarters for the owner's family. Ask the zoning officer which one governs

value.name: One more dwelling unit at or above the second story (RR, by special exception)
value.conditions: RR permits the RP uses by special exception (205-152C(2)). Among them is one dwelling unit at or above the second story, as an accessory use of a permitted use such as a single-family detached dwelling (205-46A, I)
value.note: Read literally, a house in RR may hold one more dwelling unit at or above the second story after a Zoning Hearing Board special exception, with no family rule. This conflicts with the family-only relative quarters of 205-16B(4). Ask the zoning officer which one governs

value.name: Townhouse or twin house development (BR-1)
value.conditions: 'When approved as a conditional use, a townhouse and/or twin house may be approved' on a tract with at least 60,000 sq ft of contiguous lot area, at most 5.5 dwelling units per net lot area, and otherwise under the CR rules of 205-37 to 205-41 (205-30.2B). The intent is a density no higher than one unit per 7,500 sq ft of net lot area (205-30.1)
value.note: A development of a whole tract by the Board of Supervisors, not a second unit on one house lot

value.name: Dwellings at or above the second story with a commercial use (C, C-1)
value.conditions: 'Accessory uses on the same lot with and customarily incidental to any of the above permitted uses, including dwellings, provided that such accessory uses shall be located at or above the second-story level.' Lot 15,000 sq ft, building area 40%, front 50 ft, side 20 ft (60 ft next to a residential or institutional district), rear 50 ft, height 35 ft. Two off-street spaces per dwelling unit (205-102A)
value.note: The host is a retail, service or office use, not a house

value.name: Residential units above the first floor of a nonresidential use (SC)
value.conditions: Residential units on the second floor and above only, not on a floor with other uses, at least 650 sq ft, at most two bedrooms, separate entrance, parking within 300 ft, site plan approval before a building permit (205-68O). A shopping center needs at least two acres (205-69C)

value.name: Dwellings accessory to a business or professional use (BP)
value.conditions: 'Accessory uses on the same lot with and customarily incidental to any of the above permitted uses, including dwellings' by conditional use from the Board of Supervisors (205-62B, 205-22). Lot 30,000 sq ft, building area 30%, front 50 ft, side 20 ft (25 ft next to a residential or institutional district), rear 50 ft, height 35 ft
value.note: The host is an office or other BP use, not a house

historic_bypass.note: No historic ADU path found in the zoning chapter

districts_in_doubt.note: This district's own use list does not plainly put relative quarters with a house

districts_read_no_listing.note: No house with 205-16 accessory uses. BP permits dwellings accessory to its uses only by conditional use. C and C-1 permit dwellings at or above the second story with a commercial use, SC residential units above the first floor, EC and ECII apartment houses and ECII townhouses, twins, duplexes and triplexes with 205-16 uses barred (205-63.12A). I, LI and HI permit no dwelling. ATR permits age-targeted housing with only a no-impact home-based business as an accessory use

value.condition: Only the property owner and members of his or her immediate family may occupy the house and the quarters. The owner may not lease or rent the quarters as an apartment or separate dwelling.
The quarters are in the existing house or attached to it, with a standard doorway or passageway always kept between the house and the quarters. Not in a separate freestanding building.

The owner files a deed restriction with the Recorder of Deeds, in a form the Township Solicitor accepts, setting out these conditions. The property is sold only as a single-family dwelling with the whole structure. On a sale, unless the deed restriction is filed and the buyer keeps the relative quarters, any second kitchen is removed first. A one-year renewable permit from the Zoning Officer.

In an AR subdivision of 80 acres or more developed under 205-26, with public water and sewer, lots may be up to 25% smaller than 20,000 sq ft but never under 15,000 sq ft, with width 75 ft, front yard 40 ft, side yards 15 ft each, rear yard 45 ft and building coverage 20%. These figures replace the AR figures on such a lot.

reading.value: Two off-street spaces for the house, a garage not counted. Four if the relative quarters count as a second dwelling unit. The code does not say which.
